title: Madrid office gets connection timed out in Teams
scenario: A customer relays what other teams told her instead of what she checked: DNS, proxies, service health and token state are all said to be fine; the engineer tests each, confirms three and finds that the proxy dashboard is wrong about one node and that the network did change.

events.title: Madrid timeouts, Teams
events.text: Hello, our Madrid office (about 60 people) gets the message connection timed out when opening Teams since Friday afternoon. Barcelona is fine. I am only passing on what I was told: the network team says all three DNS servers answer fine and all four proxy nodes are green on their dashboard; our helpdesk says the Microsoft status page is green; the desktop team says the token state is healthy on the laptops. I have not checked any of it myself. The network team also says nothing was changed on the network.

events.title: Re: Madrid timeouts, Teams
events.text: Hello Lucía, thank you for saying clearly who said what. I will test those points myself instead of relying on them. Please send me the names of three affected users and the UTC moment of one failure each.

events.title: Re: Madrid timeouts, Teams
events.text: Users: c.ortega 08:12 UTC, j.molina 08:41 UTC, r.navarro 09:05 UTC.

events.title: Sign-in log lookup
events.text: Looked up the three users in the Entra sign-in logs at the times given. There is no failure row for any of them.

events.title: Service health
events.text: Service health at 09:30 UTC: nothing active for Teams or Entra ID.

events.title: Name resolution by server
events.text: From a Madrid PC I resolved login.microsoftonline.com against each of the three DNS servers, ten times each. All three answered every time, within milliseconds.

events.title: Per-proxy test
events.text: Requested the sign-in host through each of the four Madrid proxy nodes, five times each. mad-prx1, mad-prx2 and mad-prx4 answered in under a second. mad-prx3 timed out after 30 s on all five.

events.title: What I found
events.text: I tested the points. DNS is fine, as the network team said, and service health is clear. The proxy dashboard is wrong, though: mad-prx3 times out on the Microsoft sign-in address, and the other three nodes answer normally. Please ask the network team what changed on the proxy cluster, because the statement that nothing changed may not hold.

events.title: Re: What I found
events.text: I looked again. The security team pushed a new TLS inspection profile to the proxy cluster last Thursday evening and I was not told. mad-prx3 took the profile but its certificate store is full. I am taking mad-prx3 out of the pool now.

events.title: Re: What I found
events.text: mad-prx3 has been out since 11:20 UTC. At 11:55 nobody in Madrid has reported a timeout since then, I asked on all floors.

events.title: Test sign-ins
events.text: 20 of 20 test sign-ins from Madrid succeed since 11:25 UTC. Before the change about three in ten had timed out.

events.title: Closing note
events.text: Cause: one proxy node of four timed out for the Microsoft sign-in host after a TLS inspection profile was pushed without the network team knowing; the proxy dashboard still showed all nodes green. DNS, service health and the token state were as reported. Workaround: node out of the pool. The customer's security and network teams will agree how profile changes are announced.
